purpose: Crosswalk the 2016 C. macrocephalus population study's Cagayan sample localities with its public GenBank accession records, while preserving the limits on waterbody identity, coordinate precision, current presence, and reuse.

sourcesReviewed.title: Low genetic diversity in Clarias macrocephalus Günther, 1864 (Siluriformes: Clariidae) populations in the Philippines and its implications for conservation and management
sourcesReviewed.citation: Tan, M. T. C., Jumawan, J. C., & Quilang, J. P. (2016). Journal of Threatened Taxa, 8(6), 8849–8859. https://doi.org/10.11609/jott.2261.8.6.8849-8859
sourcesReviewed.reviewedSections: Abstract; sample collection and tissue extraction; DNA sequence analysis; results; article copyright and license statement.
sourcesReviewed.reuse: The article states Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International (CC BY 4.0). Credit the authors and Journal of Threatened Taxa; no article text, figure, or table is copied into the project.

sourcesReviewed.title: GenBank D-loop sequence metadata for the 120 Clarias macrocephalus samples in Tan et al. (2016)
sourcesReviewed.provider: National Center for Biotechnology Information, GenBank
sourcesReviewed.reviewedFields: Accession, organism, isolate, lat_lon, collection_date, collected_by, and identified_by across KM363261–KM363380.
sourcesReviewed.reuse: The records were consulted as public sequence metadata. Their reviewed GenBank feature fields did not state a Creative Commons license. No nucleotide sequence strings are retained in this review.

sourcesReviewed.title: Molecular Phylogeny of Catfishes in the Philippines using mitochondrial and nuclear genes
sourcesReviewed.reviewedUse: Existing independent catfish study retained as context only; its taxon sample subset is not the 120 D-loop accessions reviewed here.

sourcesReviewed.title: BOLD/iBOL Cagayan River catfish specimen and barcode records
sourcesReviewed.reviewedUse: Existing 2011 sample/process metadata retained as a separate evidence series; no specimen-level crosswalk to KM363261–KM363380 was found.

sourcesReviewed.title: Bidding Documents for the Connectivity Enhancement Program for E-Learning in Public Schools
sourcesReviewed.provider: Department of Information and Communications Technology
sourcesReviewed.reviewedUse: The December 2025 Annex A lists Paddaya ES, Buguey at 18.3148072, 121.7619903 and Simpatuyo ES, Santa Teresita at 18.2477910, 121.8956260. These are school facility points, not barangay boundaries or fish collection records.

sourcesReviewed.title: Philippine Standard Geographic Code: Barangays in Buguey
sourcesReviewed.reviewedUse: The PSGC page lists Paddaya Este and Paddaya Weste as Buguey barangays as of 31 July 2025; it does not provide boundary geometry or resolve the study coordinate.

sourcesReviewed.title: Camalaniugan Cagayan Briefer
sourcesReviewed.reviewedUse: The historical overview mentions settlement along the Cagayan River and a historical river-mouth name involving Camalaniugan, but does not tie the modern Minanga study samples to a named aquatic body or station. Not used to assign a waterbody.

study.collectionProcess: The paper reports 40 specimens from each named site and says specimens were obtained from local fishermen and fish vendors. It describes morphological identification and DNA barcoding context. This is source-reported sample provenance, not a standardized reach-level fish survey.

coordinateLocalityAudit.interpretation: The DICT document lists these school locations by municipality, and PSA lists Paddaya Este/Weste as Buguey barangays. Facility points do not define barangay boundaries or fish origins, so this mismatch flags a source-locality/coordinate conflict but does not prove which field is wrong. Keep the article locality and GenBank coordinate as separate source claims; do not map the 18.26, 121.89 point as Paddaya until independently reconciled.

sites.sourceLocality: San Marcos, Bunawan, Agusan del Sur
sites.scopeNote: Included only to reconcile the article's full 120-record accession series; outside Region II.

study.sequenceDescription: The article says the 120 sequences cover the complete mitochondrial DNA control region (870 bp) and were submitted to GenBank as KM363261–KM363380. The accession range query returned 120 records. The 80 Cagayan records split evenly across the two article-named sites, with matching article/GenBank coordinate strings and dated GenBank collection metadata.

crossStudyOverlap.earlierCOIAccessions: The 2016 paper separately discusses five Cagayan COI accessions, KF604662–KF604666, as a prior DNA-barcoding comparison. Those are not the KM363261–KM363380 D-loop accession range. No specimen-level mapping between the two accession series was established; do not add the five COI records to the 80 Cagayan D-loop sample count.
crossStudyOverlap.2011BOLDRecords: The existing BOLD review covers 2011 sample/process records. These are a separate source series by date and accession family; no per-specimen crosswalk to the 2012–2014 KM series was found. Keep the records separate and do not sum them as one survey.

qualityAndReuseLimits: The study names Paddaya and Minanga localities and gives coordinates, but it does not name the river, lake, lagoon, or other waterbody from which each fish was obtained. Do not infer a waterbody from nearby geography or a municipality name.

For Paddaya, the article and GenBank both report 18.26 N, 121.89 E, but the official DICT school-location annex places its Paddaya ES point about 14.8 km away and a Santa Teresita school point about 1.5 km away. These facility points are not administrative boundaries or fish-source records; preserve the conflict and hold the Paddaya coordinate from mapping pending reconciliation.

The article says specimens came from local fishermen and fish vendors. The evidence does not describe a standardized wild sampling effort or guarantee that every specimen was caught at the reported coordinate.

The article and GenBank provide coordinates rounded to 0.01 degree; no coordinate uncertainty field or reach-level boundary was established. Treat them as source-reported locality coordinates, not precise fishing locations or map geometry.
No museum voucher or specimen-depository crosswalk for these 120 KM accessions was identified in the reviewed article and GenBank fields.

The accessions and dated sample metadata support historical research provenance only; they do not establish present-day occupancy, abundance, catchability, diet, habitat suitability, legal access, or food safety.
The article's 2016 conservation-status discussion refers to contemporary sources at that time; it is not copied as a current status claim.
Article reuse is CC BY 4.0 with attribution. GenBank records are handled as accessioned public metadata here; no raw sequences, article images, tables, or copied article text are included.
No app species row, public occurrence row, survey-event row, coordinate, geometry, current safety/legal/diet statement, or product content is approved by this research review.
nextAction: Keep the Paddaya coordinate/locality conflict and both unnamed waterbodies unresolved; continue with independent Region II freshwater sources so this one crosswalk does not delay broader coverage. Revisit author/depositor clarification only if a precise site is needed.
